newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Channel 5 TV station to launch in March.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Channel 5 TV station to launch in March.

text.p: Britain's fifth terrestrial television channel said on Friday it would launch on March 30 next year -- three months later than originally planned.
The Easter Sunday debut has been agreed between Channel 5 and watchdog body the Independent Television Commission (ITC).

The launch was delayed to allow Channel 5's "retuners" time to complete the task of visiting some 10 million households up and down the country to adjust video recorders which face possible interference from the network's signal.
Their workload was increased last month when Channel 5 was granted access to a new broadcast frequency which will boost its coverage to 80 percent of Britain.
"The business is looking stronger than ever with wider coverage than we originally planned," Channel 5 chief executive David Elstein said on Friday.

"The task of visiting all the homes in our coverage area and retuning if necessary is well underway, with over one million homes completed, 3,000 retuners in action and over 2,000 more trained and ready to be deployed."
Channel 5 is a consortium comprising British media groups Pearson and United News & Media, plus Luxembourg broadcaster CLT and U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus.

Forecast to capture around five percent of all viewing, it will be Britain's third commercial television channel, joining the mainstream ITV network and Channel 4 which has a special remit to cater for minority interests.
The two BBC channels are funded by an annual licence fee paid by all television set owners.
